claims.text: Admission documentation records active suicidal ideation with plan and intent.
Admission documentation records a stated plan to overdose before admission, following a goodbye note written on October 31.
Risk assessment at admission documents a preparatory act in the past week.
The 2026-11-01 progress note assessed the patient as high risk and stated continued need for inpatient level of care.
On 2026-11-01 the patient was on close observation.
Observation was reduced to every 15 minutes on November 2, as documented in the 2026-11-03 progress note.
On 2026-11-03 the patient reported passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent.
Risk remains moderate given recent preparatory act, ambivalence about safety after discharge, and living alone.
On 2026-11-03 the patient's mood was depressed with a slightly brighter affect and limited future orientation.
The 2026-11-03 progress note documented partial improvement.
On 2026-11-03 the patient attended 2 of 4 groups.
The patient ate 25% of meals on 2026-11-01 and 50% of meals on 2026-11-03.
A family meeting had not been held as of 2026-11-03 because the sibling was unavailable until November 4.
On 2026-11-01 the patient was tearful and stated I still want to die.
The patient was diagnosed with major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe, without psychotic features at admission.
At admission the patient reported two weeks of worsening depressed mood after job loss.
The patient reported sleeping 3 to 4 hours a night before admission, and the 2026-11-01 note recorded 3 hours of sleep.
The patient had an 8-pound weight loss and poor appetite before admission.
The patient has a history of hypothyroidism, which is treated.
Urine drug screen was negative at admission.
At admission the patient was documented as disheveled with poor insight and judgment.
Before admission the patient was nonadherent to sertraline for six weeks and outpatient therapy had stopped in July 2026.
The patient had one prior inpatient admission in 2021 for suicidal ideation.
The patient lives alone in an apartment, and the sibling lives 40 minutes away.

Documented 2026-11-03 findings describe partial improvement in mood, affect, sleep and meal intake alongside continued suicidal ideation, a recent preparatory act and living-situation factors; the clinician should weigh these together.

openQuestions: No progress note for 2026-11-02 is in the supplied records, so the observation reduction referenced in the 2026-11-03 note cannot be verified from a daily note.
No discharge plan is documented; the initial treatment plan states the discharge plan is to be determined, and the 2026-11-03 note states only to begin discharge planning.
The initial treatment plan shows no signature, date of review, or update after 2026-11-01.

Sertraline dose history conflicts across records: the intake lists a prior prescription of 100 mg, the treatment plan restarts 50 mg, and the 2026-11-03 note increases to 100 mg. Not reconciled; clinician to clarify.
Intent is described differently across the 2026-11-01 intake and progress note; not reconciled; clinician to review.

The concurrent review request is marked as a draft, and no submission or signature is documented in the supplied records. The authorization record states a concurrent review deadline; clinician to confirm submission status.
Completion of the family meeting and written safety plan is not documented beyond plans to hold them.
